title: ‘Balcanica,’ Starring Matilda De Angelis, Picked Up by M-Appeal Ahead of Venice World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Berlin-based sales outfit M-Appeal has picked up international sales rights to Nicola Sorcinelli‘s “Balcanica,” starring Matilda De Angelis, which w
body:
Berlin-based sales outfit M-Appeal has picked up international sales rights to Nicola Sorcinelli‘s “Balcanica,” starring Matilda De Angelis, which will have its world premiere in competition at the 23rd Giornate degli Autori, also known as Venice Days, held alongside the 83rd Venice Intl. Film Festival.

	“Balcanica” follows the journey of the orchestra conductor Nasar and his tuba-playing son Jalil across the Balkans, after leaving Afghanistan, where music has been banned. Their path eventually crosses that of Greta, an Italian doctor whose empathy and resilience shine through the situation. As their journeys continue to intertwine, the three must face the life changing choices the moment demands.
	

	The film stars Italian actress Matilda De Angelis, known for her leading role in the Netflix series “The Law According to Lidia Poët,” Silver Bear winner Babak Karimi, celebrated for his performance in Asghar Farhadi’s “A Separation,” winner of the Golden Bear at the 2011 Berlinale and the 2012 Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, and rising talent Ivar Wafaei. The screenplay is written by Sorcinelli and Andrea Brusa.


	“Balcanica” is produced by Nightswim and Fremantle’s Wildside, in co-production with This and That Productions and Antitalent, and in association with M74 and Nieminen Film.

	Sorcinelli said that “Balcanica,” her debut feature film, is “a story about a vital journey, denied freedoms and the deeply human need to keep searching for one’s place in the world. Bringing it to Venice is a joy that is difficult to put into words.”

	Maren Kroymann, CEO of M-Appeal, described the film as “a powerful story of human connection and empathy in impossible situations.” She added that Sorcinelli “has crafted a timely, emotional and universal story that deserves to be seen everywhere, brought to life by an incredible cast.”

title: Matthew Macfadyen and Claire Foy to Lead Adaptation of David Nicholls’ ‘You Are Here’ for BBC and Starz
description:
Matthew Macfadyen and Claire Foy are to lead the TV adaptation of “You Are Here,” the bestselling novel by “One Day” author David Nicholls. 

	The 8
body:
Matthew Macfadyen and Claire Foy are to lead the TV adaptation of “You Are Here,” the bestselling novel by “One Day” author David Nicholls. 

	The 8-part series — which was first announced by Variety earlier this year — has been green lit by the BBC and Starz, with Lenny Abrahamson directing, reuniting with the BBC for the first time since “Normal People.” Set to be filmed around in the Lake District and around Manchester, “You Are Here,” is being produced by the Fremantle-owned Irish powerhouse Element Pictures, who also produced “Normal People.” Global sales will be handled by Fremantle with De Maio Entertainment spearheading the partnership with Starz.
	

	Set along the Coast to Coast walking trail from the Lake District to Robin Hood’s Bay in North Yorkshire, “You Are Here” follows Michael (Macfadyen) and Marnie (Foy), strangers thrown together by a mutual friend who unexpectedly find themselves setting off on an epic walk. Against the odds, they end up on the brink of a relationship that neither was looking for, but which might be exactly the one they both need.


	The series is “about finding a connection when you least expect it and overcoming the obstacles of midlife,” reads the description. “Treading the tricky path from loneliness to love, Marnie and Michael go coast-to-coast across the stunning (and sometimes soaking) English countryside, navigating an undeniable attraction that is as exhilarating as it is terrifying.”

	“I’m so delighted to be working on ‘You Are Here’ with Element, the BBC, Starz and Lenny, whose work I’ve admired for many years,” said Nicholls, who adapted his own novel. “And Matthew and Claire are both just dream casting, wonderful in comedy and drama, so detailed and thoughtful and sympathetic. The intention with the novel was to write a close-up study of a relationship, but set against this magnificent landscape, and that’s our ambition here too; to make something both intimate and epic, funny and dramatic, a romantic comedy with real emotion. We can’t wait to bring Marnie and Michael’s journey to the screen.”
	

	Added Abrahamson: “As a huge admirer of David’s writing, I’m delighted to be collaborating with him to bring ‘You Are Here’ to the screen. The novel is such a beautiful love story – funny, profound and ultimately deeply hopeful. I’m also extremely excited to have Claire and Matthew, two actors I hugely admire, playing Michael and Marnie.”

	“You Are Here” is an Element Pictures, a Fremantle company, production for the BBC and Starz. Both Abrahamson and Nicholls serve as executive producers alongside Claire Foy and MacFadyen, Ed Guiney, Andrew Lowe and Emma Norton for Element Pictures and Jonny Richards and Anna Ferguson for the BBC. The series is produced by Clare Shepherd.

title: Busan’s Asian Project Market Unveils 30 Selections for 2026 Edition
description:
Busan’s Asian Project Market (APM) has unveiled the 30 feature projects selected for its 2026 edition.

	APM set a new all-time submissions record f
body:
Busan’s Asian Project Market (APM) has unveiled the 30 feature projects selected for its 2026 edition.

	APM set a new all-time submissions record for the third consecutive year, receiving 604 entries from 48 countries. That marked an increase of 149 submissions year-on-year, following 455 submissions from 44 countries in 2025, 441 from 44 countries in 2024 and 399 from 50 countries in 2023. Submissions from Asia reached 423, up 82 from the previous year, while Korean submissions rose to 137, up 58.
	

	From that pool, 30 projects representing 20 countries were selected. The lineup spans courtroom drama, coming-of-age story, family drama, crime thriller, queer romantic comedy, black comedy and mystery thriller, with the selected works touching on social realities, personal identity, family relationships and ethical tensions within communities. The slate mixes feature debuts from emerging filmmakers with new projects from directors already recognized on the festival circuit.


	Three Japanese projects made the cut: “13” from Mori Tatsuya, who claimed BIFF’s New Currents prize in 2023 for “September 1923”; “Wings of Return (working title)” from Hirose Nanako; and “Yours” from Igarashi Kohei.

	Central and South Asian filmmakers also feature prominently. Kyrgyzstan’s Dastan Zhapar Ryskeldi joins APM for a third time with “Bosogo,” while Sri Lanka’s Prasanna Vithanage presents “Islands,” following “Paradise,” which took the Jiseok prize at BIFF in 2023. India’s Dominic Sangma brings “Veil of Dust,” examining tragic contradictions within a community, and Tribeny Rai returns with her second project, “A Chronicle of Minor Things” (working title). Rounding out the region are Payal Sethi’s “Babak,” Stenzin Tankyong’s feature debut “Idiot (Kakthet)” and Pakistani director Eshah Shakeel’s feature debut “Dancers.”
	

	China, Hong Kong and Taiwan contributed four selections, pairing emerging filmmakers with experienced producers. Tibetan director Kangdrun presents “Orlo in the House,” Wang Zhiyi brings feature debut “Unripe,” Hong Kong’s So Chak Long enters with “Whisper of the Silence” and Taiwan’s Yen Hao-hsuan makes his first feature with “Uncle.”

	Southeast and West Asian entries include Aditya Ahmad’s feature directorial debut “Goldfish.” Ahmad previously took the top short-film prize in Venice’s Horizons sidebar in 2018. Reza Rahadian Matulessy follows debut feature “On Your Lap,” which picked up three prizes in BIFF’s Vision – Asia sidebar in 2025, with second feature “Casparina.” Cambodia’s Chheangkea has his first feature, “Little Phnom Penh,” selected, while the Philippines’ E Del Mundo brings “Once Upon a Time in the Philippines” and Iran’s Mehrnoush Alia presents “Bon Voyage.” Singapore’s Alvin Lee offers black comedy “Talk To Me When You Are Dead,” and Malaysia’s Tan Seng Kiat presents “One Fine Day,” which took the APM Next prize at TCCF 2025. Also selected are Thailand’s Panu Aree with “Fātimah” and Indonesia’s Mouly Surya with “The Wife Who Can See Dead People (Or Jinn).”

	Seven Korean projects round out the slate. Lee Sangcheol, whose films “Jesus Hospital,” “The Snob” and “Blesser” have all screened at BIFF, presents “PARK Deul-bi.” Choi Hyunyoung, whose “Memories of a Dead End” played in Korean Cinema Today – Panorama, brings “All’s Well That Ends Well,” and Lee Hanju, whose debut feature “The Waves of Winter” screened in the Korean Cinema Today – Vision strand, presents “The Family Table.” The remaining Korean selections are Park Syeyoung’s “Satellite of Love,” Park Joonho’s “Kuroshio” (Park also directed “3670”), actor-director Ryu Hyunkyung’s “Dog Fight” and novelist-filmmaker Kim Jinyeong’s “Red Hunger”; Kim previously directed “The Other Child.” The seven projects span psychological thriller, queer romantic comedy, black comedy, mystery thriller and drama.

	Selected projects will be nominated for awards backed by sponsors.

	ACFM is the official market of the Busan International Film Festival and is held in Busan every October. The 2025 edition, ACFM’s 20th, drew industry professionals from 55 countries – 3,024 of them, alongside 1,222 registered companies – with on-site attendance reaching a record 30,006. The Sales Market tallied 8,438 business meetings, generating an estimated $71.1 million in transactions.
	

	The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with the 21st ACFM held Oct. 10-13.

title: Giorgio Armani Series in the Works From Fremantle-Owned Lux Vide and Iconic Designer’s Fashion House (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The life and career of Giorgio Armani is set to be the subject of a high-end TV series produced by Italy’s Lux Vide, which is collaborating with the
body:
The life and career of Giorgio Armani is set to be the subject of a high-end TV series produced by Italy’s Lux Vide, which is collaborating with the fashion house founded by the iconic designer known for his close ties to Hollywood.

	The still-untitled Armani biopic series — which will be tailored for the international market — has enlisted Turkish-born Italy-based director Ferzan Ozpetek, who is known for combining artistic depth with box-office appeal.
	

	Ozpetek, who knew Armani personally, recently scored a global hit with the 2025 crowdpleaser “Diamonds,” about a group of warm-hearted women in a Rome atelier rushing to fulfill a demanding order from an Oscar-winning costume designer client in the 1970s. “Diamonds” scored mightily at the box local office and traveled widely. Ozpetek’s TV experience includes 2022’s first Disney+ Italian original series “The Ignorant Angels,” a romantic drama spun off from his local hit “Ignorant Fairies.”


	“I knew, admired and spent time with Giorgio for many years, both on official occasions and in more private settings,” Ozpetek said in a statement to Variety. “We talked about cinema, of which he was notably passionate and an expert. But also about art, costumes, architecture, and, I would say, life itself. I could see within him a visionary and a brilliant artist. But also a down-to-earth and very determined man.”

	The director added: “The opportunity to tell his story is both an exciting honor and a challenge that involves capturing the many facets of such a complex, original and captivating personality.”
	

	Ozpetek is co-writing the screenplay for the Armani series in collaboration with Lux Vide’s head writer Francesco Arlanch, whose credits include Lux’s widely exported series “Medici,” “Hotel Costiera” and medical drama “Doc.” Storylines and series structure are being kept under wraps.

	Known globally as the Milan-based fashion pioneer with piercing blue eyes and a vision that combined laid back elegance and attention to detail, Armani first made his mark with the unlined men’s sports jackets and deconstructed suits worn by Richard Gere in 1980 in “American Gigolo.” But Armani also reimagined the woman’s power suit. He dressed scores of Hollywood’s female stars including Julia Roberts, Diane Keaton, Jodie Foster, Cate Blanchett, Lupita Nyong’o, Anne Hathaway and Michelle Yeoh in both minimalist attire — such as the Armani men’s suit famously worn by Julia Roberts when she won a Golden Globe for “Steel Magnolias” in 1990 — and glittery gowns like the “Nairobi blue” crystal-encrusted sequin gown worn by Lupita Nyong’o at the 2024 Academy Awards. The long list of male actors who regularly wore Armani on red carpets, and also on screen, comprises Leonardo DiCaprio, George Clooney Russell Crowe, Robert De Niro and Tom Cruise, to name a few.  

	His Hollywood connection earned Armani wardrobe film credits in more than 200 movies. 

	Armani — a self-made man who fully owned his $10 billion fashion empire at the time of his death on Sept. 4, 2025 at age 91 – was known to often appear in dark trousers and his trademark black T-shirt. He was born in the northern Italian town of Piacenza on July 11, 1934. After two decades in the fashion industry starting in 1957, he and his partner Sergio Galeotti sold their Volkswagen for $10,000 to start up their own menswear ready-to-wear label. They launched both men’s and women’s lines the following year.

	Fiercely private, Armani rarely discussed his personal life. He did tell Vanity Fair that he had romances with both men and women. He was in long-term relationship with Galeotti until his AIDS-related death in 1985.

	The Giorgio Armani fashion house has agreed to support production of the Fremantle TV series, providing access to its “archives, creations and iconic locations, offering an unparalleled insight into the world and legacy of one of fashion’s most influential figures,” according to a Fremantle statement.
	

	“For years, Lux had been chasing the dream of telling the world the story of Giorgio Armani, an artist who invented a unique and recognizeable style,” Lux Vide founder and president Matilde Bernabei said in a statement. She went on to describe Armani as “a standard-bearer of Made in Italy who rewrote the rules of style and elegance.”

	“It will be an ambitious series,” Bernabei added, “and we are proud to know that the market has immediately embraced this project with interest, enthusiastically confirming its international potential.”



	

					Giorgio Armani and Ferzan Ozpetek
									Stefano Guindani/Courtesy Armani

title: Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “La Mesías,” the multi-prized series created by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, behind the Cannes best-director winning “La bola negra,” will be r
body:
“La Mesías,” the multi-prized series created by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, behind the Cannes best-director winning “La bola negra,” will be released by Mubi in U.K., Canada, Turkey, the Netherlands, Germany and Austria and Australia, streaming exclusively from Sept. 3.

	A Movistar Plus Original, produced in collaboration with Ambrossi and Calvo’s  label Suma Content, “La Mesías” will also stream on Mubi in France, Mubi announced Thursday. The deal was closed with Movistar Plus International. Mubi will launch with a two-episode premiere.
	

	A step-up from “Veneno,” which made a splash on HBO in the U.S., six-part series “La Mesías” delivered a example of the full-on ambition of Los Javis, as Ambrossi and Calvo are known in Spain, which was seen again in “La bola negra,” one of the highest-profile Cannes main competition contenders which sparked rave reviews, and a bidding war for the U.S. rights. 


	“La Mesías,” Los Javis’ title just prior to “La bola negra,” begins with thirtysomething loner Enric watching a viral video of Stella Maris, a Christian pop band. His reaction? He literally wets himself. For the singers are his younger sisters. Memories flood back of his own childhood and youth, traumatized by his parents’ religious fanaticism which climaxes in mother Montse declaring herself the daughter of God, and that the words her daughters sing are dictated to her by God and part of her mission to save humanity via music. 

	Enric escaped. He now determines to save his sisters. Action flashes back and forward from a present-day 2013 to the 1980s when Enric and slightly younger sister Irene are kids, to around 1997, catching them in their late teens. 
	

	The production shot for 25 weeks totally on location, mostly at 30 rural sites outside Barcelona. The series featured 170 characters and 3,800 extras. 1980s flashbacks are sometimes lensed in 16 mm, capturing the impressionism of memory. The series genre hops: Episode 1 blends psychodrama and sci-fi, for example. Ep. 2 has a procedural pulse; Episode 3 works like a real-life musical.

	For all its style, the series delivers a powerful sense of the importance of family education. 

	To mark Mubi’s release announcement, it has shared with Variety a new international trailer, which captures Enric (Roger Casamayor, “Pan’s Labyrinth”) as he seeks out sister Irene (Macarena García), literally scarred by the past, to help him rescue his sisters, plus the presentation of an early video, “lyrics by God,” says one little sister, and later bizarre Christian pop rap, created by Spanish underground duo Carlos Ballesteros and Genís Segarra. Rosalía producer Raül Refree composed the series’ original soundtrack. 



	Messianic matriarch Montse is played at different ages by Ana Rujas (“Cardo”), Cannes best actress winner Lola Dueñas (“Volver,” “La bola negra”) and Carmen Machi, star of Series Mania winner “Celeste.”   

	“It’s very difficult to unlearn what you’ve been taught – I’m talking about education – the past resounds in your body for ever. That touches me in many ways. As a son, a member of the LGBT collective. The series talks about religion, but as a form of education and this is what makes it interesting,” Javier Calvo said on a Variety set visit to the isolated family house, hidden in wooded mountains south of Barcelona. 

	“La Mesías” world premiered at San Sebastián Festival in 2023, where it gleaned glowing reviews. It went on to become the first Spanish series to be selected for the Sundance Festival, win direction and a Student Audience Award at Series Mania and, released by Arte France, be hailed by La Liberation as “one of the most beautiful series of the year.”

	Picked up off Cannes by Netflix, “La bola negra” is now being positioned as an awards contender. 



	

					Macarena García as Irene in ‘La Mesías’      Credit Lucia Faraig

schema.headline: Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Ramayana’ Trailer: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash Face Off in First Part of Nitesh Tiwari’s Epic
description: The first trailer for “Ramayana” has debuted, marking the most substantial promotional asset yet for Nitesh Tiwari‘s two-part adaptation of the anci
body:
The first trailer for “Ramayana” has debuted, marking the most substantial promotional asset yet for Nitesh Tiwari‘s two-part adaptation of the ancient Hindu epic, ahead of a worldwide release this November.

	The story follows exiled prince Rama (Ranbir Kapoor) and his consort Sita (Sai Pallavi) through exile into catastrophe, as Sita’s abduction at the hands of Ravana (Yash) sets in motion an epic war between righteousness and evil. Part 1 is expected to culminate with the abduction itself, leaving the rescue campaign and the climactic battle for Part 2. Both parts are filmed for Imax.  The two films together are budgeted at approximately $500 million, Variety understands.
	

	The long-awaited trailer offers a sweeping first look at the Hindi-language spectacle, which will also be dubbed into several other languages. 


	The preview opens with an introduction to demon king Ravana asserting his dominion across the three realms of heaven, earth, and the underworld. A voiceover establishes the overarching mythological conflict, explaining how Lord Vishnu takes human form to restore righteousness on earth when chaos threatens the universe, introducing Kapoor’s Prince Rama as King Dasharatha’s eldest son.

	The trailer shifts focus to Rama’s 14-year exile to the forest to uphold his father’s vow, accompanied by his wife Sita and brother Lakshmana (played by Ravi Dubey). The peaceful exile is shattered when Ravana’s sister, Surpanakha (played by Rakul Preet Singh), becomes infatuated with Rama, setting off a chain of events that leads to her humiliation. Vowing retribution, Ravana steps in to restore his pride, initiating the conflict that leads to Sita’s abduction.
	

	Building to a grand finale, the footage showcases high-scale visual effects, mythological weaponry, and massive army battles as Rama vows to defeat Ravana across the three worlds and rescue Sita, signaling the start of the era of Rama.

	Kapoor, Yash, Tiwari and Namit Malhotra, founder of Prime Focus and DNEG CEO, appeared at San Diego Comic-Con to debut the new clip and discuss the making of the epic movies.

	“Ramayana” Part 1 is set to open during the Diwali holiday frame, with Part 2 following on Diwali 2027. The choice of release window is no accident. Diwali – one of the most widely observed festivals in the Hindu calendar – marks the return of Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and his victory over Ravana. The lighting of lamps that defines the celebration is said to represent the illumination of Ayodhya on the night its beloved prince came home.

	Score duties are shared by Oscar-winning composers Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman. DNEG – the eight-time Oscar winning VFX house, whose credits include the “Dune” movies, “Interstellar” and “Inception” – is handling visual effects. Tiwari, whose “Dangal” remains the highest-grossing Indian film ever made, directs from a screenplay by Shridhar Raghavan.

	Sony Pictures is handling international distribution for all territories outside India and Dharma Productions within India.

	Watch the trailer here:

title: Joyce Carol Oates Defends ‘The Odyssey’ and Slams Translator for Scathing Review: ‘Speaks in the Crude Language of MAGA Folks’
description: Author Joyce Carol Oates came to the defense of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” after translator Emily Wilson wrote a viral review attacking the f
body:
Author Joyce Carol Oates came to the defense of Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” after translator Emily Wilson wrote a viral review attacking the film.

	“Rather than disagreeing with interpretations of Homer in a collegial manner, this person, who has benefited enormously from Nolan’s film, speaks in the crude language of MAGA folks attacking someone with ideas that differ from hers,” Carol wrote on X. “One would expect a translator, of all people, beholden to a text, in service to a text, to be just a wee bit more thoughtful & respectful of others who are acting in good faith just as (she would claim) she is.”
	

	Wilson, who translated a 2017 version of Homer’s “The Odyssey,” slammed Nolan’s take in a review for the London Review of Books. She wrote that the film lacked “psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth” and had “nothing convincing to say.”


	Wilson’s review reads, “I had hoped that Nolan’s affinity with these Homeric themes might push him to new creative heights, and enable him to conjure more believable characters. But ‘The Odyssey’ features his usual combination of grandiosity and superficiality … the film’s vision is too confused, its characters too underdeveloped, to deliver what it half-promises in terms of big ideas – although it is very good at conveying big bangs and big giants.”

	She later added, “The writing is abysmal. None of the characters has a convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible.”

	Nolan previously praised Wilson for her translation of the ancient text. He told Empire that he used the opening line of her version, “Tell me about a complicated man,” as a north star when fleshing out Matt Damon’s role as Odysseus.

schema.headline: Joyce Carol Oates Defends ‘The Odyssey’ and Slams Translator for Scathing Review: ‘Speaks in the Crude Language of MAGA Folks’

title: Supernatural Reality Competition Korean Series ‘House of Fates’ Greenlit as ‘Battle of Fates’ Spinoff at Disney+
description: Disney+ has greenlit “House of Fates,” a spinoff of the record-breaking Korean competition series “Battle of Fates,” from the original show’s produc
body:
Disney+ has greenlit “House of Fates,” a spinoff of the record-breaking Korean competition series “Battle of Fates,” from the original show’s producer and writer.

	The new series, shot on location in Korea, is fronted by the three top-placing fate readers from “Battle of Fates,” joined at points by other contestants from the original cast. The format sends its participants around the country to sites tied to Korean spiritual practice, where they take in ceremonies, regional customs and communal meals.
	

	Along the way, cast members sit for personal fate readings and open up about relationships and losses in their own lives, then move into direct contact with shamanic ritual, a practice the format positions as central to Korean spiritual life.


	“Battle of Fates” premiered on Feb. 11 and became the No. 1 series premiere on Disney+ Korea based on views in its first 12 days. The competition series featured masters of shamanism, tarot, face and foot reading, saju and other divination disciplines competing in challenges that tested their abilities, using tools including fans, bells, dowsing rods and modern-day laptops.

	Local adaptations of “Battle of Fates” are also in development in other markets. “House of Fates” is the first spinoff greenlit by Disney+ since the original series premiered.

	“Battle of Fates” Season 1 comprises 10 episodes, all available to stream on Disney+ alongside other Korean variety titles including “I Am Boxer,” “The Zone: Survival Mission” and “My Name Is Gabriel,” starring Blackpink’s Jennie.

	Disney+ has not yet revealed a release date for “House of Fates.”

schema.headline: Supernatural Reality Competition Korean Series ‘House of Fates’ Greenlit as ‘Battle of Fates’ Spinoff at Disney+

title: Ben Affleck Wins $1 Million Prize on ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire,’ One Year After Matt Damon Did the Same
description:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for Season 5, Episode 2 of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire,” which aired on ABC at 8 p.m. ET.

	Ben Affle
body:
SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for Season 5, Episode 2 of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire,” which aired on ABC at 8 p.m. ET.

	Ben Affleck has joined the pantheon of celebrity winners of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire,” taking home the top prize with a little (or a lot) of help from “Jeopardy!” champion Jamie Ding.

	Affleck conquered the $1 million question almost exactly one year after his “Good Will Hunting” co-star and best bud Matt Damon did the same. Damon was similarly paired with a “Jeopardy!” wiz — current host Ken Jennings — who helped him reach the top prize for charity.
	

	The money from Affleck and Ding’s victory will go toward Affleck’s Eastern Congo Initiative, the first U.S.-based advocacy and grant-making organization dedicated to supporting the people living in the African region.


	In the final question, Affleck and Ding had to guess which turkeys were not pardoned by a U.S. president: A) Peanut Butter & Jelly; B) Tater & Tot; C) Mac & Cheese; D) Spaghetti & Meatball. Not knowing the answer, the contestants used their lifeline to ask host Jimmy Kimmel. While Kimmel said he was not 100% sure, he guessed the answer as Spaghetti & Meatball. Affleck and Ding then used another lifeline to phone a friend, which was Ding’s longtime trivia partner Stephen Morrison. Morrison did not know the answer either and declined to guess, which led Affleck to suggest they should go with Kimmel’s guess. “I would bet on Jimmy,” he said. “I would go for it.”

	As Ding locked in the answer, with $1 million for charity on the line, Kimmel said, “I have such a stomach ache right now.” After a long moment of suspense, the show revealed Spaghetti & Meatball to be the correct answer. As confetti rained down on the studio, Affleck and Ding jumped for joy and hugged, with genuinely shocked looks painted on their faces.
	

	Affleck and Ding are the fifth winners of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire” during Kimmel’s tenure, which began in April 2020. David Chang became the first winner of the show’s new iteration in November 2020, followed by celebrity pairs Ike and Alan Barinholtz in August 2024, Damon and Jennings in July 2025 and “The Office” stars Oscar Nuñez and Kate Flannery in September 2025.

	In July, Kimmel told Variety of the Affleck-Ding duo, “I’m not sure Ben knew that he was paired with a champion when he agreed to do the show. But when I told him, he seemed surprised and delighted. I think he was prepared to do it on his own. He’s very smart, that Ben Affleck.”

	Watch the moment Affleck and Ding won the $1 million below.

schema.headline: Ben Affleck Wins $1 Million Prize on ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire,’ One Year After Matt Damon Did the Same

title: Thanh Hang, Hong Anh’s Vietnamese Period Drama ‘Madame in Saigon’ Lands North American Rights Deal With Reel Citrus, Live On (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Reel Citrus has acquired North American rights to the Vietnamese period drama “Mesdames Thanh Sắc,” which it will release as “Madame in Saigon,” thr
body:
Reel Citrus has acquired North American rights to the Vietnamese period drama “Mesdames Thanh Sắc,” which it will release as “Madame in Saigon,” through a partnership with Ho Chi Minh City-based production and rights partner Live On. 

	Directed by Thắng Vũ, “Madame in Saigon” is set in 1960s Saigon and follows dancer Cầm Thanh (Thanh Hằng) as she rises through the city’s nightlife into a power struggle with Madame Sắc (Hồng Ánh), owner of the Kim Đô nightclub. The cast also includes Lương Thế Thành and singer-actor Văn Mai Hương. The film opened in Vietnam in June.
	

	Reel Citrus will hold a red-carpet premiere in Los Angeles on Aug. 26, with Thanh Hằng in attendance. The actor rose to fame as Vietnam’s preeminent supermodel in the 2010s before moving into dramatic film roles, with credits including “Mẹ chồng” (“Mother-in-Law”) and “Những cô gái chân dài.” She has also served as a longtime judge on “Vietnam’s Next Top Model.”


	Following the premiere, Thanh Hằng will join a press junket in Orange County alongside local community organizations. The wider campaign will extend across digital platforms and include creator support, as well as Vietnamese Student Associations across the U.S. and Canada.

	“‘Madame in Saigon’ is exactly the kind of story we built Reel Citrus to champion, bold, unapologetically Vietnamese, and made to travel,” said Brittany Tran, executive director of Reel Citrus.

	“Our job is to build the audience around the film to make sure our communities see themselves on screen and show up for each other. Partnering with Live On to bring this film and Thanh Hằng to North American audiences is a milestone for us, and just the beginning,” Tran added.
	

	Founded in 2025, Reel Citrus has previously led theatrical marketing campaigns for “Leaving Mom” and “Ancestral Home.” Its next release, “Summer School, 2001,” is slated for October.

	The deal marks Live On’s first U.S. collaboration and its debut in the North American theatrical market. The Ho Chi Minh City studio has spent more than a decade producing multi-genre Vietnamese films.

	The film opens across North America on Aug. 28.

schema.headline: Thanh Hang, Hong Anh’s Vietnamese Period Drama ‘Madame in Saigon’ Lands North American Rights Deal With Reel Citrus, Live On (EXCLUSIVE)

            Taylor Frankie Paul is telling her exes "hell no" when it comes to their latest child custody proposals because she would get to see her kiddos less than 50 percent of the time, according to a new report. 
      
    
            Citing a source, the New York Post says "The Secret Lives of Mormon Lives" star recently received two separate custody agreements from her childrens' fathers, Dakota Mortensen and Tate Paul, with the men asking for 60 percent of custody to Taylor's 40 percent.

            Taylor was married to Tate from 2016 to 2022, and they share an 8-year-old daughter, Indy, and a 6-year-old son, Ocean.  As for Dakota, he dated Taylor from 2022 to 2026, and they have one son, 2-year-old Ever. 
      
    
            The source also said Taylor is digging in for a long court battle against her exes who she now believes are in cahoots to win primary custody of the kids. But the source adds that Taylor "can't wait to witness them lose" in court.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In March, Dakota won full custody of Ever and was issued a protective order after geting into several physical altercations with Taylor, who was also granted a protective order. In June, Tate filed a temporary restraining order against Taylor and a petition seeking sole custody of their kids.

title: Mackenzie Shirilla Takes Fight for New Trial to Federal Court
description:
Mackenzie Shirilla
                          Wants Feds to Give Her a New Trial
body:
Mackenzie Shirilla
                          Wants Feds to Give Her a New Trial
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 29, 2026
                            7:01 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Mackenzie Shirilla is taking her fight from Ohio's highest court to the feds ... launching a sweeping new challenge to the murder convictions that landed her in prison.
      
    
            According to a federal petition, obtained by TMZ, Mackenzie is asking a judge to throw out her convictions and order a new trial ... challenging nearly every part of the case against her.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Her attorney, Steven Bradley, argues there wasn't enough evidence to move Mackenzie's case from juvenile to adult court -- she was 17 when she crashed -- or convict her of intentionally killing her boyfriend, Dominic Russo, and their friend, Davion Flanagan.
      

            Bradley also claims Mackenzie's trial attorneys failed to present evidence suggesting Dominic may have grabbed the steering wheel before the car slammed into a building at around 100 MPH.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The petition further claims her lawyers failed to fully investigate her nervous-system disorder -- which can cause fainting and dizziness -- or call an expert to explain how it may have caused her to lose consciousness behind the wheel.
      
    
            Mackenzie is also challenging changes made to the victims' coroner reports, as well as testimony from a medical examiner who allegedly did not personally perform either autopsy.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The federal filing comes after the Ohio Supreme Court declined to hear her appeal ... a request to reconsider that decision remains pending.
      
    
            She's serving two concurrent sentences of 15 years to life and will first be eligible for parole in 2037.
